title: National Workshop on "Mission Zero –  Ending Fatalities in Sanitation Work"
subtitle:
Achieving zero fatalities in sanitation work is a core national priority under the vision of the Hon’ble Prime Minister Narendra Modi; Need for a whole-of-government approach to ensure safe, systematic and dignified sanitation services: Secretary Sudhansh Pant
NAMASTE, GARIMA schemes to promote mechanisation and ensure occupational safety, health, education and livelihood opportunities for sanitation workers, their dependents.
body_text:
As part of strengthening institutional mechanisms, promoting appropriate technologies, ensuring operational preparedness and scaling up mechanised sanitation services across cities in the country, a National Workshop on “Mission Zero: Ending Fatalities in Sanitation Work” was organised at the State Convention Centre, Lokseva Bhawan, Bhubaneswar in Odisha today.
The workshop was graced by Shri Mohan Charan Majhi, Hon’ble Chief Minister of Odisha. Among the other dignitaries present were Shri Sudhansh Pant,  Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment, Government of India; Smt. Anu Garg, Chief Secretary, Govt. of Odisha, Smt. Usha Padhee, Additional Chief Secretary, Housing & Urban Development Department, Government of Odisha; Shri V. K. Chaurasia, Advisor, CPHEEO; Shri Debabrata Mohanty, Managing Director, WATCO; Shri Prabhat Kumar Singh, Managing Director, NSKFDC, the nodal agency for implementation of NAMASTE; Ms. Meghna Malhotra and Shri Xerxes Rao, UMC; Shri Chanchal Rana, IAS, Municipal Commissioner, Bhubaneswar Municipal Corporation; and Dr. Vijay Suryavansi, IAS, Municipal Commissioner, Pimpri Chinchwad Municipal Corporation.
Senior government officials, Urban Local Bodies (ULBs), sanitation-sector experts, manufacturers, technology providers, civil society organisations and sanitation workers to deliberate on building a safe, dignified and fully mechanised sanitation ecosystem.
The workshop focused on strengthening institutional mechanisms, promoting appropriate technologies, ensuring operational preparedness and scaling up mechanised sanitation services across cities, with the overarching objective of achieving zero fatalities in sanitation work.
Talking to media, Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment, Shri Sudhansh Pant reiterated that achieving zero fatalities in sanitation work is a core national priority under the vision of the Hon’ble Prime Minister Narendra Modi. He emphasised the need for a whole-of-government approach to ensure that sanitation services are delivered safely, systematically and with dignity.

The participation of diverse stakeholders underscored the importance of coordinated action among governments, ULBs, technology providers and communities to eliminate hazardous manual sanitation practices.
The workshop reaffirmed the collective commitment to building a safe, dignified, technology-driven and sustainable sanitation ecosystem, where no sanitation worker loses their life while performing sanitation duties.
The Mission Zero approach seeks to transform sanitation work through mechanisation, institutional preparedness, worker safety, social security and livelihood support, paving the way towards zero fatalities in sanitation work across the country.

enrichment.summary: A National Workshop titled 'Mission Zero: Ending Fatalities in Sanitation Work' was held in Bhubaneswar, Odisha, bringing together central and state officials, ULBs, technology providers and sanitation workers to discuss mechanisation and safety in sanitation work. Secretary Sudhansh Pant of the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment stated that achieving zero fatalities in sanitation work is a core national priority, calling for a whole-of-government approach. The workshop referenced the NAMASTE and GARIMA schemes as vehicles for mechanisation, occupational safety, health, education and livelihood support for sanitation workers and their dependents.
enrichment.context: Manual scavenging and hazardous manual cleaning of sewers and septic tanks remain a serious occupational safety and social justice issue in India, despite the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013. NAMASTE (National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem), launched jointly by the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment and Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, aims to eliminate hazardous manual cleaning of sewers and septic tanks by promoting mechanisation, worker registration, PPE kits, health insurance and skill development. GARIMA is a related scheme focused on the welfare and dignity of safai karamcharis and their dependents. This workshop appears to be a stakeholder consultation/awareness event reinforcing implementation of these existing schemes rather than announcing new policy, funding or legislative changes.

prelims_questions.question: The 'NAMASTE' scheme, referred to in the context of sanitation worker safety, is jointly implemented by the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment and which other ministry?
options: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
prelims_questions.explanation: NAMASTE (National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem) is a joint initiative of the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment and the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs aimed at mechanising sanitation work and eliminating hazardous manual cleaning.

prelims_questions.question: Which legislation seeks to prohibit the employment of persons as manual scavengers and provides for their rehabilitation in India?
options: The Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013
The Building and Other Construction Workers Act, 1996
The Unorganised Workers' Social Security Act, 2008
prelims_questions.explanation: The 2013 Act prohibits manual scavenging and provides for rehabilitation of manual scavengers, forming the legal backbone for schemes like NAMASTE that aim at mechanisation and worker safety.

mains_questions.question: Despite legal prohibition, hazardous manual cleaning of sewers and septic tanks continues in India. Discuss the institutional and technological measures needed to achieve 'zero fatalities' in sanitation work.
Examine the role of schemes like NAMASTE and GARIMA in ensuring dignity, safety and livelihood security for sanitation workers in India.

study_notes.reason: The release names concrete, testable schemes (NAMASTE, GARIMA, implementing agency NSKFDC) while also reinforcing a persistent GS2/GS3 governance issue — manual scavenging elimination — that supports analytical questions on mechanisation and social justice implementation gaps.

prelims.point: NAMASTE (National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem) is jointly implemented by the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment and Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs to eliminate hazardous manual cleaning of sewers/septic tanks.
prelims.why_important: A dual-ministry scheme is a classic UPSC distractor point testing which ministries jointly run a programme.

prelims.point: NSKFDC (National Safai Karamcharis Finance & Development Corporation) is the nodal implementing agency for NAMASTE.
prelims.why_important: UPSC often tests the specific nodal/implementing agency of a scheme rather than just its name.

prelims.point: GARIMA is a scheme for welfare and dignity of safai karamcharis and their dependents, distinct from but complementary to NAMASTE.
prelims.why_important: Distinguishing NAMASTE (mechanisation/safety) from GARIMA (welfare/dignity) is a likely prelims-style comparison.

prelims.point: The Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013 is the legal backdrop against which schemes like NAMASTE operate.
prelims.why_important: Aspirants should know the legislative basis underlying sanitation worker protection schemes.

mains.point: Persistent fatalities in manual sanitation work despite a 2013 law reflect a gap between legislative prohibition and ground-level implementation.
mains.analytical_use: Useful for answers on why legal prohibition of manual scavenging has not translated into elimination of deaths, examining enforcement, mechanisation and municipal capacity gaps.

mains.point: Achieving 'zero fatalities' requires a whole-of-government approach spanning central ministries, state governments and Urban Local Bodies.
mains.analytical_use: Can be used to discuss coordination challenges between multiple levels of government in delivering a welfare/safety mission.

mains.point: Mechanisation of sanitation work is positioned as the primary technological solution to eliminate hazardous manual cleaning.
mains.analytical_use: Supports 'suggest measures' type questions on using technology to address occupational hazards and dignity of labour.
